_README: The lines a queue stage's agent sees on its task card at the end of every turn (the proxy's cooperative
route), under 'Done when'. Keep them few and short: the proxy keeps at most 8 lines, 240 characters each,
1000 in all. {KEY} is the ticket's key. Keys starting with _ are not read. A reminder.md with an
{{INSTRUCTIONS}} line gets them there instead of on the card.
plan: This stage: PLAN. Change no code; run no build or test. Read the code the ticket touches, then write the plan file in the card's shape.
Each criterion is ONE line: - ACn: GIVEN .. WHEN .. THEN .. ending (ticket: "exact words") or (edge of ACn); cover every edge case of each one.
Every decision the ticket and the code leave open is a Question with Options and a Default, not a guess.
Then the self-check: read back each file and function your Steps name, fix the plan, write it again. Not done before that.
implement: This stage: IMPLEMENT the plan's Steps, one todo item each (file, function, its ACs, edge cases included).

Do NOT write or run tests, or install anything, in this stage: each item's check step is the build only, the project's build/compile/lint command, else a syntax check of each changed file (bash -n, python -m py_compile, node --check).
Run it, read the output, fix what you broke. Finish only when the card's Done line holds and the build is clean.
review: This stage: REVIEW. Change no code, commit nothing, write or run no tests.
One todo item per AC of the plan, edge cases included: find the lines that meet it (path:line); one no code meets is a Must fix item.
Then check correctness, security, scope, simplicity, write the review file in the card's shape, and finish.
fix: This stage: FIX the Must fix items only, one todo item each (path:line and the fix); change nothing else.

Do NOT write or run tests, or install anything, in this stage: each item's check step is the build only, the project's build/compile/lint command, else a syntax check of each changed file (bash -n, python -m py_compile, node --check).
Finish only when the card's Done line holds and the build is clean.
plan+test: This stage: PLAN. Change no code; run no build or test. Read the code the ticket touches, then write the plan file in the card's shape.
Each criterion is ONE line: - ACn: GIVEN .. WHEN .. THEN .. ending (ticket: "exact words") or (edge of ACn); cover every edge case of each one.
Every decision the ticket and the code leave open is a Question with Options and a Default, not a guess.
Then the self-check: read back each file and function your Steps name, fix the plan, write it again. Not done before that.

A test stage writes tests from your criteria next: no test files in Steps; add ## Tests with - Command: `<the test command>` and - Files: `<test files>`. No test framework found: a [blocking] Question.
test: This stage: TEST. Write the tests for the plan's criteria before the code exists; change no other file. Use the project's own test framework only; install nothing, set up no new one.
One todo item per AC, edge cases included: a test that checks its THEN, with a comment naming its ACn. Call the code as the plan's Steps name it: it does not exist yet.
Each item's check step is a syntax check of the test file (python -m py_compile, bash -n, node --check), not a run: the tests are meant to fail until the implement stage.
No test framework in the project: commit nothing and finish with the summary NO TEST FRAMEWORK: <what you looked for, where>.
implement+test: This stage: IMPLEMENT the plan's Steps, one todo item each (file, function, its ACs, edge cases included).
The test stage already wrote the tests. Each item's check step: run {TEST}, read the output, fix the code. Do NOT edit, skip or delete those tests, and write no new ones.
Install nothing. A test that contradicts the plan, or {TEST} cannot run here: leave it, and say which and why in the commit message.
Finish only when the card's Done line holds and {TEST} passes.
review+test: This stage: REVIEW. Change no code, commit nothing, write no tests.
Run {TEST} once and read the output: each failing test is a Must fix item (test name, the error).
One todo item per AC of the plan, edge cases included: find the lines that meet it (path:line); one no code meets is a Must fix item.
An AC with no test, or a test the implement stage changed without a reason the plan bears out: a Must fix item.
Then check correctness, security, scope, simplicity, write the review file in the card's shape, and finish.
fix+test: This stage: FIX the Must fix items only, one todo item each (path:line and the fix); change nothing else.
Each item's check step: run {TEST}, read the output. Change a test only where its Must fix item says it is wrong; write no new tests, install nothing.
Finish only when the card's Done line holds and {TEST} passes.
